package_info.why_malicious: The md-to-pdf package (version 4.1.0) is vulnerable due to its use of the gray-matter library, which exposes a JavaScript engine by default. This allows arbitrary JavaScript code execution when parsing user-supplied Markdown with front matter, leading to a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability. Attackers can exploit this to execute arbitrary code on the server, such as reading sensitive files (e.g., /flag.txt).

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user-supplied Markdown processed for PDF export)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when user-supplied Markdown is processed for PDF export, the code executes arbitrary JavaScript via the gray-matter front matter parser, reads the contents of /flag.txt using Node.js fs.readFileSync, and injects the flag value into the generated PDF, resulting in sensitive data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code leverages a Markdown front matter feature to execute arbitrary JavaScript on the server, which is highly abnormal and dangerous. It directly accesses sensitive files and exposes their contents to the user.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, Markdown-to-PDF conversion should only process markup and not execute arbitrary code. The expected behavior is safe rendering of user input, not server-side code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Server-side code execution via Markdown front matter is never legitimate in production. In rare cases, trusted admin-only environments might use such features for advanced templating, but never with untrusted input.
key_indicators: Arbitrary JavaScript execution via Markdown front matter
Injection of sensitive file contents into user-facing output
No input sanitization or code execution restrictions

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits specially crafted Markdown with JavaScript front matter to the invoice generator.
attack_chain.leads_to: Server parses the Markdown and executes the embedded JavaScript.

attack_chain.action: The malicious JavaScript reads the contents of /flag.txt using Node.js fs.readFileSync.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data (flag) is loaded into memory.

attack_chain.action: The code injects the flag value into the CSS of the generated PDF.
attack_chain.leads_to: Flag is exfiltrated to the attacker via the exported PDF.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of arbitrary JavaScript during Markdown-to-PDF conversion
Access to sensitive files (e.g., /flag.txt) from within Markdown processing
User-controlled input leading to server-side code execution
file_indicators: Markdown files or input containing ---js front matter blocks
References to require('fs') or other Node.js modules in user-supplied content
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections initiated during Markdown processing (if exfiltration is attempted via network)
No direct network indicators in this specific exploit, but possible in variants
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the use of ---js front matter in Markdown inputs, especially when processed by md-to-pdf or gray-matter. Audit application logs for unexpected file access (e.g., /flag.txt) during document generation. Use static analysis to detect unsafe use of gray-matter with JS engine enabled. Block or sanitize user-supplied front matter in Markdown, and upgrade md-to-pdf to a version that disables arbitrary code execution.
